title: ETHChiangmai & Longevity Hackathon 2026
description:
ETHChiangmai & Longevity Hackathon 2026 brings together builders from Web3, AI and Longevity in Chiang Mai on December 26–27. Over two days, teams of 1–4 will build real products for real people, from stablecoin payments used by local merchants to tools that help people sleep, move and live better. PayFi & RWA (3,000 USDT): bring stablecoins and onchain assets into everyday life: payments, crypto cards, merchant acceptance, remittances, real-world assets, and agentic payments.

Longevity (3,000 USDT): an open, product-focused track with no Web3 requirement. Build around movement, sleep, biohacking and peptides, including AI health companions.

Privacy & Data Sovereignty (3,000 USDT): give people real ownership of their data through ZK, FHE, private identity, health data sovereignty and private AI.

Cosmo-Localism (Bonus, 1,000 USDT): build for real users in Southeast Asia. It can be combined with any other track. AI is welcome in every track, and any tech stack is welcome. Whether you’re a developer, designer, researcher or health enthusiast, come build with a global community in one of the world’s favourite cities for digital nomads. title: haxfinity
description:
3–4 JANUARY 2027

10:30 AM, 3 December – 10:30 AM, 4 December

Amal College of Advanced Studies (Autonomous), Nilambur, Kerala Prizes:Exciting prizes — details to be announced

Team size:2–4 participants

Participation: Free Build real solutions, solve meaningful problems, and create something that works. HAXFINITY is a 24-hour hackathon conducted as part of XTHRON ’27, the annual IT fest of the Department of Computer Science, Amal College of Advanced Studies (Autonomous), Nilambur. Students from different colleges and backgrounds will identify problems, build software prototypes, and present their work to judges. The event includes the opening ceremony, a 21-hour project-building window, demonstrations, judging, and awards. There is no compulsory theme. Teams may choose any problem and build a software solution using any suitable technology. Build a product, tool, or prototype that solves a real problem or explores an idea. Build an application using machine learning, generative AI, NLP, computer vision, data analysis, or another AI-related technology. Build technology that improves people’s lives — for example, in education, healthcare, accessibility, sustainability, financial inclusion, or community welfare. Detailed judging criteria will be published before the event. Building window:*11:00 AM, 3 – 8:00 AM, 4 JANUARY (21 hours). Students from all colleges, streams, and experience levels are welcome. You can participate as a beginner, developer, designer, or creative problem-solver. Interests in AI, cybersecurity, web, mobile, cloud, or social-impact technology are all welcome. Amal College of Advanced Studies (Autonomous)

Santhigramam, Eranhimangad

Nilambur, Malappuram, Kerala — 679329 Check-in and travel details will be shared with registered participants. Opportunity to demo projects to judges

Competition Rules All project-specific development must happen during the official building window. Teams may arrive with an idea, but pre-built projects cannot be submitted. Open-source libraries, APIs, datasets, and templates are allowed, subject to their licences. Teams must disclose pre-existing components and AI tools used. Generative AI and AI-assisted development tools are allowed across all tracks. Teams should submit early; late submissions may not be accepted. A working prototype or meaningful demonstration is expected. Teams must be able to explain their technology, process, third-party components, and contributions. Projects must not violate copyright, privacy, security, or applicable law. Organisers may disqualify entries for plagiarism, misconduct, unsafe content, or rule violations. All participants are expected to maintain a respectful, inclusive, and welcoming environment. Participants can approach the organising team for assistance or to report a concern. title: Makeathon 9.0
description:
Now in its ninth edition, 
MAKEATHON 9.0
 is the flagship hackathon of the Microsoft Learn Student Chapter. It brings together developers, designers, and problem solvers from across the country to turn ideas into working solutions. Through workshops, mentorship, and a focused 24-hour building experience, participants will explore real-world challenges and demonstrate what they can create together. Undergraduate and postgraduate students from all colleges, academic years, and disciplines are welcome. Teams can include students from different colleges and disciplines. A mix of skills in development, design, AI/ML, and databases is encouraged. Each team must choose one problem statement from the officially released list and build a solution that directly addresses it. Submissions will be evaluated on innovation, relevance, feasibility, and clarity. Shortlisted teams will advance to the on-campus hackathon. title: Health Hackathon 3.0
description:
VIT Bhopal University to Host Health Hackathon 3.0 in January 2027 Event invites new ideas to make healthcare better and cost less VIT Bhopal University will host Health Hackathon 3.0 on 28 and 29 January 2027. A pre-event workshop will take place on 27 January 2027. VIT Bhopal is collaborating with the Whiting School of Engineering at Johns Hopkins University for this event. Its full title is “Health Hackathon 3.0: Global Health Access Innovation Challenge – Next Generation.” New Ideas for Better Healthcare

The event has a clear aim: it seeks innovative ideas that can improve healthcare accessibility for more people, reduce costs, and enhance overall efficiency. Participants are invited to propose actionable solutions to real-world healthcare challenges. Key focus areas for submissions include:

•	Low-cost tools and technologies for healthcare delivery.

•	New ways and platforms to support mental health.

•	Application of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in healthcare solutions.

•	Tools leveraging health data analytics to identify and predict health risks. A Chance to Share and Build Ideas

Health Hackathon 3.0 invites innovators, students, and researchers to present their concepts and refine them further. The emphasis is on practical, high-impact solutions designed to reach underserved communities and individuals facing healthcare access barriers. Event Overview & Key Dates

• Main Hackathon: 28 & 29 January 2027

• Venue: VIT Bhopal University, Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh

title: CODERAVE 2.0
description:
CODE • COLLABORATE • INNOVATE - The SLIET Annual  Hackathon. Organized by Internwell SLIET Club

Venue:
 Sant Longowal Institute of Engineering and Technology (SLIET), Longowal, Punjab

Mode:
 Hybrid — Online (All India) + Offline (SLIET Campus) Coderave 2.0 is a national-level hybrid hackathon designed to bring together innovative minds, passionate developers, designers, and problem-solvers to transform ideas into impactful technology solutions. Organized by Internwell SLIET Club, this edition offers students an opportunity to demonstrate their creativity, technical expertise, teamwork, and problem-solving abilities through a competitive, time-bound development experience. The hackathon welcomes teams from colleges and universities across India through its online participation track, while SLIET students can participate in the offline campus track. Shortlisted teams will present their ideas through PPT pitches, followed by an intensive 24-hour open-source development challenge in which participants will build, test, and demonstrate their solutions. Whether you are interested in web development, app development, artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, data science, or other emerging technologies, Coderave 2.0 is your platform to innovate, collaborate, and compete. Round 1 — Registration and PPT Submission:

title: ECLIPSE 7.0
description:
ECLIPSE 7.0
 is the flagship event of the ACM Student Chapter, TIET, and a premier 
24-hour hackathon
 that draws participation from across the nation. As the chapter’s most distinguished and celebrated initiative, it serves as a dynamic platform for developers, designers, and innovators to collaborate and compete.

With expert-led workshops, dedicated mentorship, and an intense build environment, 
ECLIPSE 7.0
 is designed to cultivate innovation, enhance technical excellence, and transform ambitious ideas into impactful, real-world solutions. • The hackathon is open to students from all Colleges and Universities. • Students from all academic years are eligible to participate. Teams may include members from different colleges. • Participants from diverse specializations are welcome to form teams together. Teams must consist of 2–5 members.

Participants are advised to form teams with complementary expertise, including design, frontend development, backend development, and database management. Each team must choose only ONE problem statement.

The detailed problem statements will be published in the PDF below and simultaneously made accessible on the ECLIPSE 7.0 website and ACM’s official social media platforms. Round 1:
 Pre-Screening Round (Online): Teams will be shortlisted based on their idea presentation. Round 2:
 Offline Hackathon Round: Shortlisted teams will participate in the on-site hackathon. During the offline round, teams will be assessed at regular checkpoints to ensure consistent progress.

All rounds must be completed within the officially communicated timelines. Physical attendance at the venue is mandatory for all qualifying participants. Required submissions for the offline round include: A code repository link and/or deployed project link and a project proposal document • Teams must register exclusively through Devfolio and provide accurate team and member details. • Teams will be evaluated only on the problem statement they have selected. Working on multiple problem statements is strictly prohibited. • The prototype must be developed strictly during the offline round. Pre-built solutions will result in disqualification. • Plagiarism is strictly prohibited and will result in immediate disqualification. • All participants are required to join the official event application and community platform. Failure to comply may result in disqualification. • Any form of misconduct or rule violation may result in disqualification at the discretion of the organizing committee. • Projects will be evaluated by a panel of judges. The decision of the judges will be final and binding. ECLIPSE 7.0

title: Techacks 5.0
description:

 is Season 05 of TecHacks: one 
24-hour hackathon, fully in person
, on one stage at Chitkara University, Punjab. Form a crew, pick a track and turn an idea into a working solution in one night, in one room. Learn from mentors, meet like-minded builders and pitch to the judges. TecHacks is a hacker community committed to inclusive tech literacy, open-source engagement and industry preparedness. title: Lean In Hacks 8.0
description:
Lean In Hacks is an 
annual flagship hackathon of Lean In IGDTUW
 - the first chapter of Lean In India. Lean In Hacks is a 
beginner-friendly hackathon
 and has a place for everyone wanting to learn, build, share, and grow in their lives through their unique ideas. Our hackathon journey started in 2020 when we conducted the first edition of Lean In Hacks to give grounds to new thoughts and tools to animate the imaginative and critical thinking side of developers. This time, 
hackers from any college
 can participate in our hackathon, which will be held in 
hybrid mode
. The only requirement is to have 
at least 1 female in your team
! Hackers will be given the 
weekend to build their product online
 and the 
top teams will be given a chance to pitch in the offline mode
. As a beginner-friendly hackathon, we offer a dedicated 
Beginner’s Track
 exclusively for first-time hackers. This track is designed as an 
ideathon
 for 
first-year students
